question: What will be the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 25,000 after 3 years at the rate of 10% p.a.?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective compound interest rate for 3 years at 10% p.a. is directly known to be 33.1%.

CI = 33.1% of Principal

CI = (33.1 / 100) × 25000

CI = 33.1 × 250 = 8275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹25,000

Rate (R) = 10% p.a.

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 
 Compound Interest Progression 25,000 Year 0 27,500 Year 1 30,250 Year 2 33,275 Year 3 
 + ₹2,500 (10%) 
 + ₹2,750 (10%) 
 + ₹3,025 (10%) Total Compound Interest = 33275 − 25000 = ₹8,275 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount (A) = 25000 × (1 + 10/100)³

⇒ A = 25000 × (11/10)³

⇒ A = 25000 × (1331/1000)

⇒ A = 25 × 1331 = 33275

⇒ CI = 33275 − 25000 = 8275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI vs SI Difference

For 2 years: Difference = P(R/100)²

For 3 years: Difference = P(R/100)²(3 + R/100)

Half-Yearly Compounding

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the Rate becomes R/2 and the Time period becomes 2T.

Rule of 72

A quick rule of thumb: the time taken to double an investment at compound interest is approximately 72 / R years.
